221: ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਮਤਿ; ਜੀਇ ਆਈ ਕਾਰਿ ॥੧॥
The teaching the Guru gave me has taken effect in my heart. ॥1॥
ਇਨ ਬਿਧਿ; ਰਾਮ ਰਮਤ. ਮਨੁ ਮਾਨਿਆ ॥
Remembering God, my mind has grown so used to it that it cannot now live without remembrance.
ਗਿਆਨ ਅੰਜਨੁ; ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦਿ ਪਛਾਨਿਆ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
Through the Guru's word I have found the spiritual eye salve that brings deep union with God. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
My mind now accepts that the one spiritual joy is above all others, and it has brought me into stillness of mind.
The pure word of praise has ended my wandering.
Dyed in the Name, my mind has turned a fast red, and Maya's colour now looks to me a fleeting pink.
God's glance of grace has fallen on me, and I have held back the poison of Maya. ॥2॥
My attention has turned back from Maya; while still at my worldly work my mind has died to Maya, and I have woken spiritually.
ਸਬਦਿ ਰਵੇ; ਮਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਸਿਉ ਲਾਗਿਆ ॥
Through the Guru's word I remember God, and my mind has formed a love for Him.
Gathering spiritual joy within, I have cast out the poison of Maya and given it up for good.
ਭਾਇ ਬਸੇ; ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਭਾਗਿਆ ॥੩॥
Dwelling in God's love, my fear of death has fled. ॥3॥
My cravings for worldly tastes are gone, the strife within has ended, and pride has ceased.
ਚਿਤੁ. ਹਰਿ ਸਿਉ ਰਾਤਾ; ਹੁਕਮਿ ਅਪਾਰਾ ॥
My heart is dyed in God, and I now abide in the will of the boundless Lord.
The rites I performed for caste and for people's regard have come to an end.
The Lord's glance of grace has fallen on me, and I have found spiritual peace. ॥4॥
ਤੁਝ ਬਿਨੁ; ਕੋਇ ਨ ਦੇਖਉ ਮੀਤੁ ॥
O Lord, apart from You I see no other true friend.
Whom else should I worship, to whom else should I offer my mind?
Whom else should I ask for counsel, at whose feet should I fall?
By whose teaching should I fix my attention? ॥5॥
I serve the Guru alone, and at the Guru's feet alone I fall.
Through the Guru I worship God and stay absorbed in His Name.
The Guru's teaching, his initiation and his love I have made the food of my soul.
By the Lord's will the seed of past deeds has sprouted, and I abide in my true home at His feet. ॥6॥
Pride is gone, and my attention rests in spiritual joy.
Spiritual light has dawned in me, and my soul is merged in the Lord's light.
The writ of the Guru's word engraved in my heart is now so plain that it cannot be erased.
I have come to know the Creator and His creation as the Creator Himself. ॥7॥
I am no pandit, nor clever, nor wise;
so I have not strayed from the road, nor gone astray in wandering.
I make no clever speeches; I have recognised the Lord's command.
O Nanak, through the true Guru's teaching I am absorbed in stillness of mind. ॥8॥1॥
In the jungle of the body, the mind is an elephant.
When the Guru is the goad on its head and the eternal word of praise its banner,
that mind is honoured and esteemed at the door of the Sovereign Lord. ॥1॥
By displaying cleverness no one comes to know that the mind has become worthy of esteem.
ਬਿਨੁ ਮਾਰੇ; ਕਿਉ ਕੀਮਤਿ ਪਾਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
Unless the mind is killed to its vices, how can it win any worth? ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
The nectar of the Name is in the house of the heart, but the thief, the mind caught in attachment, keeps stealing it.
So unruly is this mind that no one can refuse it.
The one whose nectar God Himself guards, He blesses with greatness. ॥2॥
The boundless fire of craving lies heaped in one place, in this mind.
The one to whom the Guru gives understanding has this fire quenched by the water of the Name.
ਮਨੁ ਦੇ ਲੀਆ; ਰਹਸਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਈ ॥੩॥
Whoever has received it has given his mind in exchange, and then sings God's praises with delight. ॥3॥
Without the Guru's goad, the mind is as unruly out in the forest as it is at home in family life.
Even sitting in a mountain cave, what can I say it has become?
Whether bathing in the sea at holy places or sitting on a mountain, it stays just as fearless. ॥4॥
But if this mind dies to its vices under the Guru's goad, say, who can strike it?
If it grows fearless in awe of the Guru's goad, what fear of the world can touch it?
Through the Guru's word it recognises its Protector dwelling in all three worlds. ॥5॥
One who merely said this with a clever mind has only said it with his tongue.
One who understood it under the Guru's goad has also recognised Him, settled in stillness of mind.
Beholding Him everywhere and reflecting on His virtues, his mind that cries "mine, mine" is won over. ॥6॥
In the heart where the one Lord's praise dwells there is glory, beauty and release from vices;
there the Lord, untouched by Maya, ever abides.
ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਬਿਆਪਿ ਰਹਿਆ; ਨਿਜ ਠਾਈ ॥੭॥
That heart becomes His own home, His own dwelling, and there He ever abides. ॥7॥
Many sages, the mind brought under the Guru's goad, sing the Lord's praises with love.
222: ਤਨਿ ਮਨਿ ਸੂਚੈ; ਸਾਚੁ ਸੁ ਚੀਤਿ ॥
With pure body and pure mind, joined in love, they praise the eternal Lord.
O Nanak, you too worship God, for ever and ever. ॥8॥2॥
ਨਾ ਮਨੁ ਮਰੈ; ਨ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਹੋਇ ॥
The mind does not die to craving, nor is life's aim of oneness with God fulfilled,
so long as the mind is in the grip of the vices, of ill counsel and of the sense of mine and yours.
ਮਨੁ ਮਾਨੈ; ਗੁਰ ਤੇ. ਇਕੁ ਹੋਇ ॥੧॥
When, taught by the Guru, the mind is won over, it becomes one with God. ॥1॥
God is beyond Maya's three qualities, yet is won over by high spiritual virtues;
the one who sheds his self-conceit keeps those virtues in his mind. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
So long as the mind is astray, it dwells on vice upon vice.
So long as the mind is astray, the load of vices piles up on one's head.
But when the mind is won over by the Lord's praise, it becomes attuned to the one God. ॥2॥
The mind gone astray goes again and again to the house of Maya,
and caught in lust it does not stay in its proper place.
O mortal being, steep your tongue in the nectar and worship God. ॥3॥
Fine elephants, fine horses, gold, sons and wife: attachment to these is a game of gambling.
They bring the mind great anxiety, and in the end one leaves the arena of the world having lost the game.
As unripe pieces in a game of chaupar are struck again and again, so the weak mind keeps taking the blows of vices. ॥4॥
The more wealth a person gathers, the more vices arise in the mind,
and joy and dread stand forever at his door.
But remembering God in the heart, the mind settles in stillness and enjoys spiritual peace. ॥5॥
When God casts His glance of grace, the Guru joins one to his word and unites him with the Lord.
Gathering spiritual virtues within, one burns away his faults through the Guru's word.
Turning to the Guru, a person finds the wealth of the Name. ॥6॥
Without being joined to the Name, every pain and trouble makes its home in the mind;
the foolish one who follows his own mind keeps his heart dwelling in Maya.
The one in whom, by God's grace from the start, the writ of past deeds comes to light turns to the Guru and finds deep union with God. ॥7॥
The mind empty of virtues stays fickle, running after Maya again and again.
The eternal, pure Lord does not like this filth of the mind.
O Nanak, the one who takes the Guru's refuge sings God's praises. ॥8॥3॥
Always talking of one's own greatness and comfort brings no peace.
The mind's cleverness binds one to perishable things, while He is eternal.
Those who love the sense of mine and yours all come to ruin.
Each one acts here according to the writ recorded from the start. ॥1॥
I have seen the world playing such a gamble:
ਸਭਿ ਸੁਖ ਮਾਗੈ; ਨਾਮੁ ਬਿਸਾਰੀ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
it begs for every comfort, yet forgets the Name. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
God is not seen with these eyes; were He seen, one would be moved to speak His Name.
Without seeing Him, no longing arises, and His Name cannot be spoken with yearning.
Facing the Guru, the mind settles in stillness and is absorbed in His love, and so He is seen within.
Such a person's attention rests in the service the Guru teaches, and his mind is fixed on the one God. ॥2॥
Asking for comfort while forgetting the Name, one only adds to his pain,
for he threads a garland of all the vices and wears it.
ਏਕ ਬਿਨਾ. ਝੂਠੇ; ਮੁਕਤਿ ਨ ਹੋਇ ॥
One caught in perishable things finds no release without the one Lord's Name.
The Creator Himself does all, and Himself watches the play. ॥3॥
The one who quenches the fire of craving through the Guru's word,
settled in stillness and joined in His love, has his wandering after Maya brought to an end.
Following the Guru's teaching, he keeps God's Name in his heart.
Through the word of praise he sings God's virtues. ॥4॥
The eternal Lord dwells in every body, but love for Him wakes only in one who takes the Guru's refuge.
Without the Name the mind never comes to rest in one place.
The beloved Lord is Himself won over by love;
He casts His glance of grace on the one who loves Him, and that one grasps the worth of His Name. ॥5॥
Attachment to Maya creates every entanglement,
and so the life of one who follows his own mind becomes filthy, vile and frightful.
The one who takes the path the true Guru shows has his entanglements broken.
He repeats the life-giving Name and enjoys spiritual peace within for ever. ॥6॥
The Gurmukh grasps the worth of the Name and fixes his attention on the one Lord;
he abides in his own true self and is absorbed in the eternal Lord.
He brings his round of birth and death to a halt.
ਪੂਰੇ ਗੁਰ ਤੇ; ਇਹ ਮਤਿ ਪਾਏ ॥੭॥
But this understanding he gains only from the perfect Guru. ॥7॥
I sing the praises of the Lord whose virtues have no end.
223: ਗੁਰੁ ਪੁਛਿ ਦੇਖਿਆ; ਨਾਹੀ ਦਰੁ ਹੋਰੁ ॥
I have asked my Guru and found that there is no other door of peace.
Pain and pleasure come to beings only within His will and pleasure.
Nanak, of little understanding, fixes his attention on the Lord and sings His praise. ॥8॥4॥
Maya, which sets a distance between beings and God, has made its home in the minds of the world,
and the lust, anger and pride born of it destroy their spiritual life. ॥1॥
Who is there other than Him? Nowhere is there anyone apart from Him.
ਸਭ ਮਹਿ; ਏਕੁ ਨਿਰੰਜਨੁ ਸੋਈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
In all dwells the one Lord, untouched by Maya. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
The ill counsel born of that distance keeps telling a person that Maya has a being apart from God.
Under it a being comes and goes, and dying a spiritual death is set apart from God. ॥2॥
But in earth and sky I see no second being.
In woman and man, in all the world, I see only God. ॥3॥
I behold the light of the sun and moon, the lamps of creation,
and within all, ever the same, I see only the ever-young beloved Lord. ॥4॥
In His grace the true Guru joined my mind to the Lord's feet,
and the true Guru made me understand that the one God dwells everywhere. ॥5॥
The one who faces the Guru comes to know that the one Lord, untouched by Maya, is present everywhere,
and killing his separation from God through the Guru's word, he recognises Him. ॥6॥
In all the world only the one Lord's command prevails.
From the One alone has all creation come. ॥7॥
Under Maya two paths arise, but know the one Master as present in all.
Through the Guru's word, recognise His command at work in all. ॥8॥
He who pervades all forms, all castes and all minds:
says Nanak, I praise that One alone. ॥9॥5॥
Only when a person does deeds that raise his spiritual life is he a true yogi.
How can one whose mind is weak before the vices know the secret of release? ॥1॥
He alone deserves the name of yogi who understands the right way of life:
ਪੰਚ ਮਾਰਿ; ਸਾਚੁ ਉਰਿ ਧਾਰੈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
killing the five vices, he keeps the eternal Lord in his heart. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
The one within whom God plants His eternal Name
grasps the worth of the way of union with God. ॥2॥
Heat and cold, harsh treatment and warm, home and forest are all alike to him.
The deed of singing God's praises is his ordinary work. ॥3॥
He begs one alms from the Guru's door, the word of God's praise,
and within him wake deep union with God, high awareness, and the way of remembrance. ॥4॥
ਭੈ ਰਚਿ ਰਹੈ; ਨ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਜਾਇ ॥
He stays absorbed in awe of the Lord and never steps outside it.
Who can put a value on such a yogi? He keeps his attention fixed on the Lord's feet. ॥5॥
The Lord Himself unites one with Him and ends his wandering.
By the Guru's grace a person reaches the highest spiritual state. ॥6॥
The true yogi does the service the Guru teaches and makes the Guru's word his reflection.
He kills his pride: this is that yogi's finest practice. ॥7॥
His chanting, austerity, self-discipline and reading of the Puranas are just this:
says Nanak, to absorb himself in the praise of the boundless Lord. ॥8॥6॥
Living as a householder, that yogi makes bearing others' wrongs his nature, and gentleness and contentment his daily practice.
ਰੋਗੁ ਨ ਬਿਆਪੈ; ਨਾ ਜਮ ਦੋਖੰ ॥
No disease of the vices can overpower him, and he has no fear of death.
ਮੁਕਤ ਭਏ; ਪ੍ਰਭ ਰੂਪ ਨ ਰੇਖੰ ॥੧॥
Such yogis are freed from vices, for they become one with the Lord who has no form or outline. ॥1॥
What fear can the true yogi have of the assaults of Maya's warriors?
ਰੂਖਿ ਬਿਰਖਿ; ਗ੍ਰਿਹਿ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਸੋਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
In trees and plants, at home and out in the wild, he sees only that Lord. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
The one who remembers the Lord untouched by Maya is the true yogi, and he does not fear Maya's assaults.
He stays alert at all times, for he keeps his attention fixed on the eternal Lord.
That yogi is dear to my mind. ॥2॥
With the fire of God's radiance revealed within, he burns away the net of death's dread.
His fear of old age and death is gone, and he drives out pride.
He crosses over himself and carries his ancestors across too. ॥3॥
The one who walks the path the true Guru shows becomes a true yogi.
ਭੈ ਰਚਿ ਰਹੈ; ਸੁ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਹੋਇ ॥
He walks in awe of the Lord, and so he is fearless of the vices' assaults,
for a person becomes like the one he serves. ॥4॥
224: Repeating the Name of the fearless Lord, a person becomes free of desire.
He makes the masterless belong to the Master; I am a sacrifice to such a yogi.
He is not born again and again; he ever sings the Lord's praises. ॥5॥
That yogi knows the one Lord pervading within him and outside in all the world.
Through the Guru's word he recognises his own true self.
Through the Guru's true word he goes to the Lord's door bearing the pass of praise. ॥6॥
ਸਬਦਿ ਮਰੈ; ਤਿਸੁ ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਵਾਸਾ ॥
The one who dies to his vices through the Guru's word dwells ever in his own inner self.
His hopes come to an end, and he no longer wanders.
Joined to the Guru's word, the lotus of his heart stays in bloom. ॥7॥
All that is seen in the world is seen with its hopes broken.
The poison of lust and anger, and the hunger and thirst for Maya, afflict everyone.
O Nanak, rare are those found in the world who are not ruled by hope and craving. ॥8॥7॥
The one who meets such a servant of the Lord has spiritual joy born within him.
He attains the eternal Lord, and pain does not come near him. ॥1॥
Seeing the Guru, the Lord's servant, a person's understanding becomes whole.
The dust of the Guru's feet is itself the bath at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
His eyes are sated of gazing on others' beauty, and the thread of his attention stays on the one Lord.
Tasting the sublime nectar of God's Name, his tongue becomes pure. ॥2॥
Remembering the eternal Lord becomes his daily practice,
and serving the unseen, unfathomable Lord within, his mind is sated of Maya. ॥3॥
ਜਹ ਜਹ ਦੇਖਉ; ਤਹ ਤਹ ਸਾਚਾ ॥
Wherever I look, I see the eternal Lord.
But the world, weak of mind before Maya and lacking this understanding, keeps quarrelling. ॥4॥
Only the one whom the Guru teaches comes to know that God is present everywhere.
Some rare one, facing the Guru, gains this understanding. ॥5॥
O Lord our Protector, have mercy and save Your creatures Yourself.
Without understanding from the Guru, beings are becoming beasts and ghosts. ॥6॥
The true Guru has made me understand that there is no other like the Lord.
ਕਿਸੁ ਕਹੁ ਦੇਖਿ; ਕਰਉ ਅਨ ਪੂਜਾ ॥੭॥
Tell me, seeing whom could I worship another? ॥7॥
God created the three worlds so that people might become saints.
The one who recognises his own self comes to understand this reality. ॥8॥
Through seeing the Guru, the eternal Lord dwells in the heart, and the Lord's love abides there.
ਪ੍ਰਣਵਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ; ਹਮ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਦਾਸ ॥੯॥੮॥
Nanak prays: I too am that Guru's servant. ॥9॥8॥
Brahma grew proud and did not understand the Lord's boundlessness.
When the calamity of his Vedas being stolen fell on him, he repented.
ਜਹ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਮਰੇ; ਤਹੀ ਮਨੁ ਮਾਨਿਆ ॥੧॥
When he remembered God, then his mind was convinced that God is the greatest. ॥1॥
Pride is such an evil in the world
ਜਿਸੁ ਗੁਰੁ ਮਿਲੈ; ਤਿਸੁ ਗਰਬੁ ਨਿਵਾਰੈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
that the one who meets the Guru has his pride driven out by the Guru. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
King Bali grew proud of his wealth.
He performed many sacrifices and swelled with pride.
But without asking his guru's counsel, he went down to the underworld. ॥2॥
King Harichand gave in charity and was lost in the glory it won him.
ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ. ਅੰਤੁ ਨ ਪਾਇ; ਅਭੇਵੈ ॥
Without the Guru he too could not grasp that the unfathomable Lord's virtues have no end.
God Himself leads astray, and Himself gives understanding. ॥3॥
Through ill counsel Harnakhas turned to wicked deeds.
But God, the Lord Narayan, is Himself the destroyer of pride.
He showed mercy and saved Prahlad. ॥4॥
Foolish Ravan went astray in his ignorance.
Lanka was plundered and his head too was cut off.
Through pride, without the true Guru's refuge, he was ruined. ॥5॥
Sahasbahu, Madhu and Kaitabh, and Mahikhasur were slain,
and Harnakhas was torn apart with nails.
These demons were slain for lacking the practice of devotion to the Lord. ॥6॥
Raktabij was killed and Kalnem was torn apart.
God slew the demons and saved the saints. ॥7॥
God Himself, in the form of the true Guru, reflects on the word of His own praise,
225: He Himself destroys the demons by entangling them in love of Maya,
and Himself carries across those who take the Guru's refuge, joining them to His remembrance and devotion. ॥8॥
Duryodhana drowned in pride and lost his honour.
In his pride he did not keep God, the Creator, in mind.
ਜਨ ਕਉ ਦੂਖਿ ਪਚੈ; ਦੁਖੁ ਹੋਈ ॥੯॥
Whoever brings suffering on God's servant is ruined by that suffering, and it falls on himself. ॥9॥
King Janamejaya did not understand his Guru's teaching;
falling into delusion he went astray, so how could he find peace?
He slipped only a little, and afterwards repented. ॥10॥
Kansa, Keshi and Chandur were mighty warriors, and none was their equal.
ਰਾਮੁ. ਨ ਚੀਨਿਆ; ਅਪਨੀ ਪਤਿ ਖੋਈ ॥
Yet in pride of their strength they did not understand God's play, and lost their honour.
Apart from the Creator, no one can protect anyone. ॥11॥
ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ; ਗਰਬੁ. ਨ ਮੇਟਿਆ ਜਾਇ ॥
Without taking the Guru's refuge, pride cannot be rooted out.
One who takes the Guru's teaching holds to patience, and patience is a lofty righteousness.
O Nanak, by following the Guru's teaching the Name is gained, and one sings God's praises. ॥12॥9॥
If I rub perfume and sandalwood on my body,
if I wear silk and silken clothes until they wear out,
ਬਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮ; ਕਹਾ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਵਉ ॥੧॥
yet if I am empty of God's Name, I can find peace nowhere. ॥1॥
What use is it to wear fine clothes and show them off to others?
ਬਿਨੁ ਜਗਦੀਸ; ਕਹਾ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
Without the Lord of the world, peace is found nowhere. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
ਕਾਨੀ ਕੁੰਡਲ; ਗਲਿ ਮੋਤੀਅਨ ਕੀ ਮਾਲਾ ॥
If I wear rings in my ears and a string of pearls round my neck,
and my red quilt is strewn with red flowers,
yet without remembering the Lord of the world, I can find peace nowhere. ॥2॥
If my wife is beautiful, with lovely eyes,
adorns herself in the sixteen ways and is very dear to me,
yet without remembering the Lord of the world there is only ruin, always. ॥3॥
If I have mansions to live in and a comfortable bed,
on which a gardener spreads flowers day and night,
ਬਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮ; ਸੁ ਦੇਹ ਦੁਖਾਲੀ ॥੪॥
yet without remembering God's Name this body remains a house of sorrows. ॥4॥
If I have fine horses and fine elephants, lancers and martial music,
armies, deputies and royal servants, all this show,
yet without remembering the Lord of the world these displays of power are perishable. ॥5॥
If I call myself a siddh and can summon miraculous powers at will,
wear a crowned cap and have a royal canopy over my head,
yet without remembering the Lord of the world, I can nowhere gain lasting spiritual strength. ॥6॥
If I call myself khan, emperor and king,
and can scold servants and attendants, all this show of power is perishable.
Without the support of the Guru's word, the purpose of human life is not fulfilled. ॥7॥
Pride and possessiveness, the longing to be great and own much, are forgotten only through the Guru's word.
Only by following the Guru's counsel is God recognised dwelling in the heart.
Nanak prays: O Lord, I have come to Your refuge. ॥8॥10॥
God's devotee serves the One alone and holds no other His equal.
He knows the world's disease-breeding pleasures to be bitter and gives them up.
ਭਾਇ ਮਿਲੈ; ਸਚੁ ਸਾਚੈ ਸਚੁ ਰੇ ॥੧॥
Joined in love, he merges in the eternal Lord and becomes one with Him. ॥1॥
Such is the Lord's devotee, His servant:
ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ ਮਿਲੈ; ਮਲੁ ਧੋਈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
singing God's praises he meets Him and washes away the filth of his mind. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
The heart-lotus of the whole world is turned upside down, away from remembrance.
The fire of evil understanding burns the world through and through.
Only the one who reflects on the Guru's word escapes it. ॥2॥
The bumblebee, the moth, the elephant and the fish,
and the deer: each dies reaping what it has done.
So a person caught in craving does not see his own source, God. ॥3॥
Under evil understanding, the man devoted to women dwells always on lust.
Then anger ruins the spiritual life of all who are given to vice.
Such people forget the Name and lose their honour and their sense. ॥4॥
226: One who follows his own mind lets his thoughts stray to another's home.
He is caught in the tangle of vices, and the noose of vice round his neck grows tighter.
One who walks the Guru's way escapes it by singing God's praises. ॥5॥
ਜਿਉ ਤਨੁ ਬਿਧਵਾ; ਪਰ ਕਉ ਦੇਈ ॥
As a widow gives her body to another man,
ਕਾਮਿ ਦਾਮਿ; ਚਿਤੁ ਪਰ ਵਸਿ ਸੇਈ ॥
and, caught in lust and greed for money, puts her mind too in his power,
ਬਿਨੁ ਪਿਰ. ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ; ਨ ਕਬਹੂੰ ਹੋਈ ॥੬॥
yet without her husband never finds peace. ॥6॥
The learned pandit reads scriptures over and over,
reads the Vedas and Puranas again and again and hears their compositions,
ਬਿਨੁ ਰਸ ਰਾਤੇ; ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਨਾਟਾ ॥੭॥
but until his mind delights in the relish of the Name, it dances to Maya's tune. ॥7॥
As the pied cuckoo loves the rain and thirsts for it,
as the fish delights in water,
so, O Nanak, God's devotee drinks the relish of God's Name and is satisfied. ॥8॥11॥
ਹਠੁ ਕਰਿ ਮਰੈ; ਨ ਲੇਖੈ ਪਾਵੈ ॥
One who endures bodily hardship by stubborn will gains nothing that is counted.
One who smears himself with ashes and puts on many garbs wastes that too.
Having forgotten the Name, in the end he regrets it. ॥1॥
ਤੂੰ ਮਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ; ਤੂੰ ਮਨਿ ਸੂਖ ॥
Enshrine the Lord in your mind, and enjoy spiritual bliss in your mind.
ਨਾਮੁ ਬਿਸਾਰਿ; ਸਹਹਿ ਜਮ ਦੂਖ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
Forgetting the Name, you will suffer at the hands of Death's messengers. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
If someone revels in perfume, sandalwood, aloe and camphor,
and is drunk on attachment to Maya, the highest spiritual state is far from him.
If the Name is forgotten, all this is futile, and one stays in futile efforts. ॥2॥
Even if lancers and drummers salute a person seated on the throne,
still craving for Maya only grows and lust presses hard.
ਬਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਜਾਚੇ; ਭਗਤਿ ਨ ਨਾਮੁ ॥੩॥
Without begging at God's door, neither devotion nor the Name is gained. ॥3॥
In the disputes and pride of learning, there is no union with God.
Only by giving your mind will you gain the Name, the source of comforts.
In love of other things, only painful ignorance grows. ॥4॥
ਬਿਨੁ ਦਮ ਕੇ; ਸਉਦਾ ਨਹੀ ਹਾਟ ॥
As without capital a shop cannot stock goods,
as without a ship there is no way across the sea,
so without taking the Guru's refuge one only loses and loses. ॥5॥
ਤਿਸ ਕਉ ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ; ਜਿ ਵਾਟ ਦਿਖਾਵੈ ॥
Praise, praise the perfect Guru, who shows the true way of life,
ਤਿਸ ਕਉ ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ; ਜਿ ਸਬਦੁ ਸੁਣਾਵੈ ॥
praise, praise the perfect Guru, who makes the word of God's praise heard,
ਤਿਸ ਕਉ ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ; ਜਿ ਮੇਲਿ ਮਿਲਾਵੈ ॥੬॥
praise, praise the perfect Guru, who brings one into union with God. ॥6॥
ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ ਤਿਸ ਕਉ; ਜਿਸ ਕਾ ਇਹੁ ਜੀਉ ॥
Praise that God whose gift this life is.
Through the Guru's word, reflect on His virtues again and again, and drink the life-giving relish of the Name.
In His will He will give you the honour of repeating the Name. ॥7॥
O my mother, without the Name I cannot live.
O Lord, I have come to Your refuge; may I keep repeating Your Name day and night.
O Nanak, honour comes only when one stays dyed in the Name. ॥8॥12॥
Saying "I, I" in religious garb, no one has ever formed a deep bond with God.
Only through the Guru does the mind take to devotion, and rare is the one who gives up self. ॥1॥
ਹਉ ਹਉ ਕਰਤ; ਨਹੀ ਸਚੁ ਪਾਈਐ ॥
By saying "I, I", the eternal Lord is never found.
ਹਉਮੈ ਜਾਇ; ਪਰਮ ਪਦੁ ਪਾਈਐ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
Only when pride goes is the highest spiritual state attained. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
Out of pride, kings make raid after raid on one another's lands,
they suffer in their pride, and stay in the round of birth and death. ॥2॥
The pride of one who reflects on the Guru's word departs;
he gives up his shallow, fickle understanding and destroys the five enemies. ॥3॥
Those with the eternal Lord in their hearts abide in stillness of mind,
and forming a deep bond with the King of all creation, they reach the highest spiritual state. ॥4॥
For one whose wandering the Guru ends, remembering the eternal Lord becomes his daily work,
and he keeps his attention fixed at the feet of the fearless Lord. ॥5॥
ਹਉ ਹਉ ਕਰਿ ਮਰਣਾ; ਕਿਆ ਪਾਵੈ ॥
Saying "I, I" brings only spiritual death; what other gain does one find?
ਪੂਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਭੇਟੇ; ਸੋ ਝਗਰੁ ਚੁਕਾਵੈ ॥੬॥
One who meets the perfect Guru ends this quarrel of pride within. ॥6॥
All the running about that rests on pride brings no spiritual gain.
Those who turn to the Guru receive wisdom from him and sing God's praises. ॥7॥
227: Pride binds beings in bonds and makes them wander in the round of birth and death.
O Nanak, one who worships God is kept from pride and finds peace. ॥8॥13॥
First of all, Brahma himself fell into the noose of spiritual death.
He went down to the underworld but could not find the end of the lotus he was born from.
He did not heed his Guru's command, and through wandering went astray. ॥1॥
Whoever is born and does not enshrine the Guru's word, the dread of death keeps his spiritual life from growing.
ਹਮ ਹਰਿ ਰਾਖੇ; ਗੁਰਸਬਦੁ ਬੀਚਾਰਿਆ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
God Himself saved my spiritual life, for I enshrined the Guru's word in my heart. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
All the goddesses and gods are caught in attachment to Maya.
ਕਾਲੁ ਨ ਛੋਡੈ; ਬਿਨੁ. ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ॥
This spiritual death does not let go without the service the Guru teaches.
Only the imperishable Lord, whose virtues cannot be told and whose secret cannot be found, is free of it. ॥2॥
Sultans, khans and emperors: none is to stay here for ever,
ਨਾਮਹੁ ਭੂਲੈ; ਜਮ ਕਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਸਹਨਾ ॥
but whoever strays from the Name suffers at the hands of Death.
ਮੈ ਧਰ ਨਾਮੁ; ਜਿਉ ਰਾਖਹੁ ਰਹਨਾ ॥੩॥
Your Name alone is my support, O Lord; keep me joined to it as You will, that I may stay in it. ॥3॥
Chaudhris or kings, no one has a lasting abode here.
Bankers who only amass Maya and money die a spiritual death.
ਮੈ ਧਨੁ ਦੀਜੈ; ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ॥੪॥
O Lord, give me the wealth of Your life-giving Name. ॥4॥
Subjects, their headmen, chiefs and lords:
none is seen who stays in the world for ever.
Mighty death strikes the head of the one whose heart holds attachment to Maya. ॥5॥
The One Lord alone is ever unshakeable and eternal;
ਜਿਨਿ ਕਰਿ ਸਾਜੀ; ਤਿਨਹਿ ਸਭ ਗੋਈ ॥
He who made and fashioned all creation takes it back into Himself.
ਓਹੁ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਜਾਪੈ; ਤਾਂ ਪਤਿ ਹੋਈ ॥੬॥
When through the Guru He is seen everywhere, then one receives honour. ॥6॥
They may be called qazis and sheikhs, or fakirs in grand garb,
and be called great in the world, but if the pain of pride is in the body,
ਕਾਲੁ ਨ ਛੋਡੈ; ਬਿਨੁ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਧੀਰਾ ॥੭॥
spiritual death does not let go without the support the true Guru gives. ॥7॥
Through the tongue in slander, through the eyes gazing at another's beauty,
and through the ears hearing deadly words, the net of spiritual death stays spread over beings.
Without the Guru's word, people are robbed of their virtues day and night. ॥8॥
One in whose heart the eternal Lord dwells, who stays in God's Name,
ਕਾਲੁ. ਨ ਜੋਹਿ ਸਕੈ; ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ ॥
spiritual death cannot even look at him, for he sings God's praises.
O Nanak, turning to the Guru, he stays merged in God through the Guru's word. ॥9॥14॥
Those who speak only the word that lasts, with not a grain of falsehood,
who, turning to the Guru, walk in the command of the Lord of the will,
stay in the refuge of the eternal Lord and remain above Maya's sway. ॥1॥
ਸਚ ਘਰਿ ਬੈਸੈ; ਕਾਲੁ ਨ ਜੋਹੈ ॥
One who stays at the feet of the eternal Lord is not touched by the dread of death.
ਮਨਮੁਖ ਕਉ; ਆਵਤ ਜਾਵਤ ਦੁਖੁ ਮੋਹੈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
But one who follows his own mind is held down by the pain of birth and death through attachment. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
Let anyone drink the relish of the Name, and by praising the Lord of endless virtues
ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਬੈਸਿ; ਸਹਜ ਘਰੁ ਲਹੀਐ ॥
one can stay in one's own true home, and there find the abode of stillness of mind.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸਿ ਮਾਤੇ; ਇਹੁ ਸੁਖੁ ਕਹੀਐ ॥੨॥
Drunk on the relish of God's Name, one can say: this is the true peace. ॥2॥
The way of life of the Guru's counsel is steady; attachment to Maya cannot shake it.
One who, by the Guru's counsel, praises God while resting in the eternal Lord in stillness of mind,
drinks the life-giving relish and churns out the reality. ॥3॥
One who has seen the true Guru and taken his teaching,
enshrined it within and offered mind and body for it,
has recognised his own source and understood God's highest state and boundless greatness. ॥4॥
One who makes the excellent Name of the stainless Lord his food
becomes an eternal supreme swan, and the light of the boundless Lord shines within him.
Wherever he looks, he sees the One Lord alone. ॥5॥
He stays untouched by Maya, and remembering the eternal Lord becomes his daily work.
ਪਰਮ ਪਦੁ ਪਾਇਆ; ਸੇਵਾ ਗੁਰ ਚਰਣੀ ॥
Doing the service the Guru teaches and staying at the Guru's feet, he attains the highest spiritual state.
ਮਨ ਤੇ ਮਨੁ ਮਾਨਿਆ; ਚੂਕੀ ਅਹੰ ਭ੍ਰਮਣੀ ॥੬॥
Within, his mind takes to remembrance, and his wandering of pride comes to an end. ॥6॥
ਇਨ ਬਿਧਿ; ਕਉਣੁ ਕਉਣੁ ਨਹੀ ਤਾਰਿਆ ॥
Whom has this way not carried across?
God's praise has carried all the saints and devotees across.
228: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਪਾਏ; ਹਮ. ਅਵਰੁ ਨ ਭਾਰਿਆ ॥੭॥
Those who praised Him found the Lord; I too seek no other. ॥7॥
One to whom the Guru, bringing him to the eternal Lord's palace, has revealed the unseen Lord in his heart
gains that unshakeable abode on which Maya casts no shadow.
Those who, joined to the eternal Lord, are sated of Maya have their wandering ended. ॥8॥
ਜਿਨ ਕੈ ਮਨਿ ਵਸਿਆ ਸਚੁ ਸੋਈ ॥
Those in whose minds the eternal Lord dwells:
their company is gained by one who takes the Guru's refuge.
O Nanak, joined to the eternal Name, he washes away his filth. ॥9॥15॥
ਰਾਮਿ ਨਾਮਿ; ਚਿਤੁ ਰਾਪੈ ਜਾ ਕਾ ॥
One whose mind is dyed in God and in His Name:
his sight should be sought on rising every morning. ॥1॥
If you do not remember God, it is your own misfortune.
ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਦਾਤਾ; ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਰਾਮੁ ਹਮਾਰਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
God, our Lord, has always been the giver to us all. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
One who repeats God's Name by the Guru's teaching becomes complete.
In his heart there is constant bloom, as if trumpets play without a break. ॥2॥
ਜੋ ਜਨ; ਰਾਮ ਭਗਤਿ ਹਰਿ ਪਿਆਰਿ ॥
Those people who are joined in love of devotion to God,
God in His mercy has saved them. ॥3॥
ਜਿਨ ਕੈ ਹਿਰਦੈ; ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਸੋਈ ॥
Those in whose hearts that Lord dwells,
ਤਿਨ ਕਾ ਦਰਸੁ ਪਰਸਿ; ਸੁਖੁ ਹੋਈ ॥੪॥
by the sight of them spiritual bliss is found. ॥4॥
The One Lord pervades all beings.
One who follows his own mind deals with beings in pride and wanders again through births. ॥5॥
One who finds the true Guru understands this;
he kills his pride and through the Guru's word attains union with God. ॥6॥
ਅਰਧ ਉਰਧ ਕੀ ਸੰਧਿ; ਕਿਉ ਜਾਨੈ ॥
Without remembrance, how can one know the meeting of the soul and God?
Only one who joins the company of Gurmukhs knows it, and his mind takes to remembrance. ॥7॥
ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਨਿਰਗੁਣ ਕਉ; ਗੁਣੁ ਕਰੀਐ ॥
O Lord, we are sinful and without virtue; give us the virtue of remembering Your Name.
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਨਾਨਕ ਜਨ ਤਰੀਐ ॥੮॥੧੬॥
O Nanak, say: O Lord, when You are merciful, Your servants can cross over. ॥8॥16॥
One Creator, realised by the Guru's grace
ਜਿਉ ਗਾਈ ਕਉ ਗੋਇਲੀ; ਰਾਖਹਿ ਕਰਿ ਸਾਰਾ ॥
As the herdsman guards the cows, so You care for beings and protect them.
ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪਾਲਹਿ ਰਾਖਿ ਲੇਹਿ; ਆਤਮ ਸੁਖੁ ਧਾਰਾ ॥੧॥
Day and night You nourish and protect them and grant them spiritual peace. ॥1॥
O Lord, merciful to the meek, protect me here and hereafter.
I have come to Your refuge; look on me with a glance of grace. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
ਜਹ ਦੇਖਉ. ਤਹ ਰਵਿ ਰਹੇ; ਰਖੁ ਰਾਖਨਹਾਰਾ ॥
O Protector Lord, wherever I look You are present, the protector of all.
ਤੂੰ ਦਾਤਾ. ਭੁਗਤਾ ਤੂੰਹੈ; ਤੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਾਣ ਅਧਾਰਾ ॥੨॥
You are the giver, You Yourself the enjoyer, You the support of every life. ॥2॥
ਕਿਰਤੁ ਪਇਆ, ਅਧ ਊਰਧੀ; ਬਿਨੁ ਗਿਆਨ ਬੀਚਾਰਾ ॥
Without wisdom and reflection, a being bound by the impressions of his own deeds now falls to the depths, now rises to the skies.
ਬਿਨੁ ਉਪਮਾ ਜਗਦੀਸ ਕੀ; ਬਿਨਸੈ ਨ. ਅੰਧਿਆਰਾ ॥੩॥
Without praise of the Lord of the world, his ignorance is not dispelled. ॥3॥
ਜਗੁ ਬਿਨਸਤ. ਹਮ ਦੇਖਿਆ; ਲੋਭੇ ਅਹੰਕਾਰਾ ॥
Daily we see the world dying a spiritual death in the grip of greed and pride.
ਗੁਰ ਸੇਵਾ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ; ਸਚੁ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਦੁਆਰਾ ॥੪॥
By the service the Guru teaches the eternal Lord is found, and the way of release is found. ॥4॥
ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਮਹਲੁ. ਅਪਾਰ ਕੋ; ਅਪਰੰਪਰੁ ਸੋਈ ॥
The abode of the boundless Lord is within one's own self; He is beyond all beyond.
ਬਿਨੁ ਸਬਦੈ. ਥਿਰੁ ਕੋ ਨਹੀ; ਬੂਝੈ ਸੁਖੁ ਹੋਈ ॥੫॥
Without the Guru's word no one stays steady there; one who understands the word finds bliss. ॥5॥
ਕਿਆ ਲੈ ਆਇਆ, ਲੇ ਜਾਇ ਕਿਆ; ਫਾਸਹਿ ਜਮ ਜਾਲਾ ॥
What did you bring, and what will you take? In vain you are caught in Death's net.
ਡੋਲੁ ਬਧਾ ਕਸਿ ਜੇਵਰੀ; ਆਕਾਸਿ ਪਤਾਲਾ ॥੬॥
Like a bucket tied to a rope, you now rise to the sky and now fall to the depths. ॥6॥
ਗੁਰਮਤਿ. ਨਾਮੁ ਨ ਵੀਸਰੈ; ਸਹਜੇ ਪਤਿ ਪਾਈਐ ॥
If by the Guru's counsel the Name is never forgotten, honour is gained in stillness of mind.
ਅੰਤਰਿ ਸਬਦੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ; ਮਿਲਿ ਆਪੁ ਗਵਾਈਐ ॥੭॥
One with the treasure of the Guru's word in his heart meets God, and meeting Him, sheds self. ॥7॥
ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇ. ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਆਪਣੀ; ਗੁਣ ਅੰਕਿ ਸਮਾਵੈ ॥
One on whom God casts His glance of grace receives His virtues and merges in His embrace.
ਨਾਨਕ ਮੇਲੁ. ਨ ਚੂਕਈ; ਲਾਹਾ ਸਚੁ ਪਾਵੈ ॥੮॥੧॥੧੭॥
O Nanak, his union with God never breaks, and he earns the true profit of God's praise. ॥8॥1॥17॥
229: ਗੁਰ ਪਰਸਾਦੀ ਬੂਝਿ ਲੇ; ਤਉ ਹੋਇ ਨਿਬੇਰਾ ॥
If by the Guru's grace you understand this, then you are released from Maya's darkness:
ਘਰਿ ਘਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਰੰਜਨਾ; ਸੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ॥੧॥
the Name of the stainless Lord dwells in every heart, and He is my Lord too. ॥1॥
ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰਸਬਦ. ਨ ਛੂਟੀਐ; ਦੇਖਹੁ ਵੀਚਾਰਾ ॥
Reflect and see: without the Guru's word there is no release.
ਜੇ ਲਖ ਕਰਮ ਕਮਾਵਹੀ; ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ. ਅੰਧਿਆਰਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
Even if you perform a hundred thousand rites, without the Guru the darkness remains. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
ਅੰਧੇ ਅਕਲੀ ਬਾਹਰੇ; ਕਿਆ ਤਿਨ ਸਿਉ ਕਹੀਐ ॥
Those blinded and robbed of sense by attachment to Maya: what use is it to tell them?
ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ. ਪੰਥੁ ਨ ਸੂਝਈ; ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ ਨਿਰਬਹੀਐ ॥੨॥
Without the Guru they cannot see the path; how can one keep company with them? ॥2॥
ਖੋਟੇ ਕਉ ਖਰਾ ਕਹੈ; ਖਰੇ. ਸਾਰ ਨ ਜਾਣੈ ॥
He calls the counterfeit genuine, and does not know the worth of the genuine wealth of the Name.
ਅੰਧੇ ਕਾ ਨਾਉ ਪਾਰਖੂ; ਕਲੀ ਕਾਲ ਵਿਡਾਣੈ ॥੩॥
The one blind in Maya is called an assessor; such is the strange way of the world in this time. ॥3॥
ਸੂਤੇ ਕਉ ਜਾਗਤੁ ਕਹੈ; ਜਾਗਤ ਕਉ ਸੂਤਾ ॥
The world calls one asleep in Maya awake, and one awake in God's remembrance asleep.
ਜੀਵਤ ਕਉ. ਮੂਆ ਕਹੈ; ਮੂਏ ਨਹੀ ਰੋਤਾ ॥੪॥
It calls the spiritually alive dead, and does not grieve for the spiritually dead. ॥4॥
ਆਵਤ ਕਉ ਜਾਤਾ ਕਹੈ; ਜਾਤੇ ਕਉ ਆਇਆ ॥
One coming onto God's path it calls lost, and one lost to God it calls the one whose coming was fruitful.
ਪਰ ਕੀ ਕਉ. ਅਪੁਨੀ ਕਹੈ; ਅਪੁਨੋ ਨਹੀ ਭਾਇਆ ॥੫॥
It calls its own the wealth that will be another's, and does not love what is truly its own. ॥5॥
ਮੀਠੇ ਕਉ ਕਉੜਾ ਕਹੈ; ਕੜੂਏ ਕਉ ਮੀਠਾ ॥
It calls the sweet relish of the Name bitter, and the bitter relish of the senses sweet.
ਰਾਤੇ ਕੀ ਨਿੰਦਾ ਕਰਹਿ; ਐਸਾ ਕਲਿ ਮਹਿ ਡੀਠਾ ॥੬॥
People slander the one dyed in the Name; such a wonder is seen in the world. ॥6॥
ਚੇਰੀ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਕਰਹਿ; ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਨਹੀ ਦੀਸੈ ॥
People serve the handmaid, Maya, but do not see her Master.
ਪੋਖਰੁ ਨੀਰੁ ਵਿਰੋਲੀਐ; ਮਾਖਨੁ ਨਹੀ ਰੀਸੈ ॥੭॥
If a pond is churned, if water is churned, no butter comes from it. ॥7॥
ਇਸੁ ਪਦ ਜੋ ਅਰਥਾਇ ਲੇਇ; ਸੋ ਗੁਰੂ ਹਮਾਰਾ ॥
One who attains this state of knowing himself, before him I bow my head.
ਨਾਨਕ ਚੀਨੈ ਆਪ ਕਉ; ਸੋ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ॥੮॥
O Nanak, one who recognises his own self becomes one with the Lord beyond Maya and without limit. ॥8॥
ਸਭੁ ਆਪੇ ਆਪਿ ਵਰਤਦਾ; ਆਪੇ ਭਰਮਾਇਆ ॥
God Himself pervades everything, and Himself leads beings astray.
ਗੁਰ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਤੇ ਬੂਝੀਐ; ਸਭੁ ਬ੍ਰਹਮੁ ਸਮਾਇਆ ॥੯॥੨॥੧੮॥
By the Guru's grace one understands that God is present everywhere. ॥9॥2॥18॥
Gauri Guareri · Ashtpadis · Guru Amar Das
One Creator, realised by the Guru's grace
Love of other things is the impurity of the mind.
Astray in wandering, one stays in the round of birth and death. ॥1॥
The impurity of one who follows his own mind never goes,
ਜਿਚਰੁ ਸਬਦਿ. ਨ ਭੀਜੈ; ਹਰਿ ਕੈ ਨਾਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
as long as he is not won over by the word and joined to God's Name. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
All this visible world and all attachment to it is the root of impurity,
and he dies and is born again and again. ॥2॥
For them there is impurity even in fire, air and water,
and impure is all the food they eat. ॥3॥
No rites and no worship can cleanse a mind gripped by impurity.
Only by being dyed in the Name does the mind become pure. ॥4॥
Taking the true Guru's support, the impurity of the mind goes;
ਮਰੈ ਨ ਜਨਮੈ; ਕਾਲੁ ਨ ਖਾਇ ॥੫॥
such a one neither dies nor is born, nor does spiritual death consume him. ॥5॥
Let anyone examine the Shastras and Smritis and see:
ਵਿਣੁ ਨਾਵੈ; ਕੋ ਮੁਕਤਿ. ਨ ਹੋਇ ॥੬॥
without the Name, no one is freed from the mind's impurity. ॥6॥
ਜੁਗ ਚਾਰੇ; ਨਾਮੁ ਉਤਮੁ ਸਬਦੁ ਬੀਚਾਰਿ ॥
In all four ages, one becomes exalted through the Name, reflecting on the Guru's word.
In this age called Kali too, only one who turns to the Guru crosses over. ॥7॥
The eternal Lord, who neither dies nor comes and goes:
O Nanak, one who turns to the Guru stays merged in Him. ॥8॥1॥
Turning to the Guru, make devotion to God the support of your life,
ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ; ਰਾਖਹੁ ਹਿਰਦੈ ਉਰ ਧਾਰਾ ॥
and keep the Lord enshrined in your heart and mind.
Through the Guru you will win honour at the eternal Lord's door. ॥1॥
O Pandit, read God's praises and give up your vices.
Through the Guru you will cross the terrifying world-ocean. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
230: By taking the Guru's refuge, pride departs from within the mind.
By taking the Guru's refuge, no filth comes to cling to the mind, for
by taking the Guru's refuge, the Name of God comes to dwell in the mind. ॥2॥
Facing the Guru, one is absorbed in the eternal Lord, and this is the true rite and duty.
One who takes the Guru's refuge burns away arrogance and the sense of mine and yours.
Dyed in the Name, one who faces the Guru receives spiritual bliss. ॥3॥
First awaken your own mind and understand that Lord.
You instruct other people, but in this way no one ever listens.
Take the Guru's refuge and understand the right way yourself, and you will have bliss for ever. ॥4॥
One who follows his own mind makes a religious show and displays great cleverness,
ਜੋ ਕਿਛੁ ਕਮਾਵੈ; ਸੁ ਥਾਇ. ਨ ਪਾਈ ॥
but whatever he actually lives out is not accepted by God.
He stays in the round of birth and death and finds no place of peace. ॥5॥
One who follows his own mind performs religious rites, and great conceit grows within him.
ਬਗ ਜਿਉ; ਲਾਇ ਬਹੈ ਨਿਤ ਧਿਆਨਾ ॥
He always sits in trance like a heron.
He will repent only when death seizes him. ॥6॥
ਬਿਨੁ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਸੇਵੇ; ਮੁਕਤਿ ਨ ਹੋਈ ॥
Without taking the true Guru's refuge, there is no release from such hypocrisy.
Only by the Guru's grace is that Lord met, who knows every heart.
In all four ages it is the Guru who gives the gift of the Name. ॥7॥
For one who takes the Guru's refuge, the Name is his high caste and lineage, and in the Name he finds his honour.
Through the Name he has cut away and cast off the hold of Maya, the ocean's daughter.
O Nanak, without the Name, all other cleverness is in vain. ॥8॥2॥
ਇਸੁ ਜੁਗ ਕਾ ਧਰਮੁ; ਪੜਹੁ ਤੁਮ ਭਾਈ ॥
O brother, learn the duty of this human birth.
The perfect Guru has given this understanding to one who takes his refuge,
that here and hereafter the Name of God is the true companion. ॥1॥
Read the praise of God and reflect on His virtues in your mind;
by the Guru's grace, wash away the filth of vices. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
By religious debate or by attacking other faiths, the Name of God is not obtained.
Caught in other tastes, mind and body grow empty of spiritual life.
ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦਿ; ਸਚਿ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਇ ॥੨॥
Only through the Guru's word can one fix one's attention on the eternal Lord. ॥2॥
Without meeting the Guru, this world is soiled by pride.
ਨਿਤ ਤੀਰਥਿ ਨਾਵੈ; ਨ ਜਾਇ ਅਹੰਕਾਰਾ ॥
It bathes daily at places of pilgrimage, yet its arrogance does not go.
ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ ਭੇਟੇ; ਜਮੁ ਕਰੇ ਖੁਆਰਾ ॥੩॥
Without meeting the Guru, spiritual death keeps it in misery. ॥3॥
ਸੋ ਜਨੁ ਸਾਚਾ; ਜਿ ਹਉਮੈ ਮਾਰੈ ॥
That person becomes one with the eternal Lord who rids himself of pride;
through the Guru's word he destroys the five vices.
He himself crosses over and carries all his family across as well. ॥4॥
As a showman stages a show, God has staged this spectacle of the world through attachment to Maya.
Those who follow their own minds, blinded by it, cling to the spectacle.
But those who face the Guru stay detached from it, their attention fixed on God. ॥5॥
One who takes religious garb for religion puts on many garbs,
but craving stays within him and he moves about in arrogance.
He does not examine his own life, and so loses the game of human birth. ॥6॥
One who wears religious garb and talks cleverly of his piety,
but through attachment to Maya is caught in great wandering and goes astray,
ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ ਸੇਵੇ; ਬਹੁਤੁ ਦੁਖੁ ਪਾਈ ॥੭॥
suffers much, because he does not take the Guru's refuge. ॥7॥
Those dyed in the Name of God remain ever detached;
while living as householders, their attention stays fixed on the eternal Lord.
O Nanak, they are greatly fortunate, for they stay in the true Guru's refuge. ॥8॥3॥
Brahma, who is held to be the founder of Vedic study,
ਤਿਸ ਤੇ ਉਪਜੇ; ਦੇਵ ਮੋਹ ਪਿਆਸਾ ॥
from him all the gods are held to have sprung, yet those gods are shown caught in attachment and the thirst for Maya.
ਤ੍ਰੈ ਗੁਣ ਭਰਮੇ; ਨਾਹੀ ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਵਾਸਾ ॥੧॥
They wandered in the three qualities of Maya and found no dwelling at the Lord's feet. ॥1॥
God has saved us from Maya and has led us to the Guru,
ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਭਗਤਿ; ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਦ੍ਰਿੜਾਇਆ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
who has fixed devotion and the Name of God firmly in our hearts at all times. ॥1॥ Rahao ॥
The word said to be composed by Brahma keeps one within the three qualities, in the snare of Maya,
ਪੜਿ ਵਾਦੁ ਵਖਾਣਹਿ; ਸਿਰਿ ਮਾਰੇ ਜਮਕਾਲਾ ॥
for scholars read it only to argue, and spiritual death keeps striking at their heads.
